notes: Performance evidence requires source-granted operation permissions and an explicit operation hash/key ID. A resend cannot add or change evidence; the first authenticated producer is retained. Plugin calls without an operation reference remain unassigned. Unknown package releases are never replaced by the latest package.
Location is an annotation: a resent event retains its first stored actor.location even when a later lookup differs. Other event facts must match.
What the Argus collector takes and how its engine reads a marker. Written by apps/api/test/sdk-contract.test.ts in argus.

ingestRequest is the body of POST /ingest/events; browserCall is the body of POST /ingest/browser; browserPayloadCall is the body of POST /ingest/browser/payloads?key=<the public key of a browser source>, one WebMCP tool run with the content its page captured, sent as JSON text while the page is open. The key is in the query, never the body, and is checked before the body is read; a call is at most 1 MiB, and a payload is truncated only when the call cannot fit otherwise, its truncated flag set.

A WebMCP tool run (kind agent.tool.executed) carries webmcp: the tool name (null where it does not match http.tool's pattern), how it ended (answered, threw, or is_error for a result that said it failed), and the JSON size of its arguments and result. Never their content, except in browserPayloadCall.

The schemas are what the collector stores. It does not refuse a call for a field they do not name: it removes the field, stores none of it and counts it on the call. Anything else they do not allow, a new value of a field they name included, refuses the call.

The collector also refuses what these schemas cannot say: an event timed more than 30 days before its call arrives, or more than a day after; an event carrying a hashed address, principal or registration in a call whose component names no hashKeyId; a fingerprint naming more than 64 components, or with a component nested more than 32 levels deep; and a string or field name anywhere in a body holding a NUL (U+0000) or half a surrogate pair.
markers.parsed is the engine reading each raw value as an agent sent it back: case ignored, "-" dropped, I and L read as 1 and O as 0.

body.stringValue: Synthetic message not selected for export.

mcpSpans.name: Transport span: mcp.<method>, or mcp.<method>:<name> for tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get (the tool, the requested resource URI without its userinfo, query or fragment, the prompt), at most 256 UTF-16 units; with no name, mcp.<method> and no colon. Handler span: mcp.<method>:<the name the tool, resource or prompt was registered under>.
mcpSpans.transport: One span per JSON-RPC message the server received, set as a step (agentrail.step true, agentrail.step.surface mcp, agentrail.step.kind tool.call for tools/call and mcp.<method> otherwise), with layer transport. protocol.version is what that message carried (its _meta, the mcp-protocol-version header, or for initialize its params), never a negotiated value; client.name and client.version are the message's own _meta clientInfo where it carries one, else what the client declared in its initialize. ERROR status for a JSON-RPC error answer, whatever raised it (jsonrpc.error_code set to the code on the wire when it is a 32-bit integer, -2147483648 to 2147483647, and omitted otherwise: the collector refuses an export carrying one outside that range), a tool result with isError (result.is_error true), a tool whose handler threw (error.type the thrown error's own type name, result.is_error kept true where the server answered the throw with an isError result of its own), or a request the transport refused with an HTTP status of 400 or more and no JSON-RPC answer.
mcpSpans.errorTypes: error.type on an ERROR span: McpJsonRpcError for a JSON-RPC error answer, tool_error for a tool result with isError (older SDKs used McpOperationError or mcp.toolResultError, which remain supported), McpTransportRejected for a request refused with no JSON-RPC answer, otherwise the thrown error's own type name. The collector reads a call's outcome in this order, the first that says one winning: a JSON-RPC error code (error); an ERROR span whose error.type is none of the tool-error names, a handler that threw (error); result.is_error true, or an ERROR span with a tool-error name (tool_error); an HTTP status of 400 or more (error). A thrown tool is a failed call, a result marked isError a failed result.
mcpSpans.standardNames: mcp.method.name on transport and handler spans; gen_ai.tool.name for tools/call and gen_ai.prompt.name for prompts/get, using the requested name on transport spans and the registered name on handler spans, bounded to 256 UTF-16 units. Resources have no name attribute: mcp.resource.uri is omitted.
mcpSpans.handler: A tool, resource or prompt callback inside a transport span: its child, layer handler, and no step (no agentrail.step). Alone, as an SDK without the transport wrapper sends it, it is the step itself and carries what a transport span would where the callback can see it: client name, version and protocol, session.id_hash, and result.is_error for a tools/call result with isError.
mcpSpans.sizes: request.bytes and response.bytes are the UTF-8 length of the JSON-RPC message as the SDK encodes it, without whitespace.
mcpSpans.requestFacts: On a step span (a transport span, or a handler span that is the step) of a message that came by HTTP: http.request.method and url.full of the HTTP request that carried it, http.response.status_code where it was answered over HTTP, user_agent.original, and the request's header facts: agentrail.http.request.header_names, the names of its headers as the server received them, comma-joined, never a value, in arrival order and case where the runtime keeps them (lower-cased, in any order, where it does not), Host included; agentrail.http.request.accept and agentrail.http.request.accept_encoding, the two headers' values as sent, each absent where the request sent none. agentrail.mcp.jsonrpc.id is the message's JSON-RPC id as text (a number in decimal), absent on a notification; gen_ai.tool.name on a tools/call names the tool asked for. A message over stdio sends none of these. Every message of a batched request carries that request's facts. The collector leaves out what a proxy adds (the names headerNames.addedOnTheWay matches) and keeps the first 40 names within 512 characters; a list holding anything but header names, an id past 128 characters, or a value holding a NUL or half a surrogate pair is not taken, and the event names it in redactions. mcpRequestFacts holds two requests as their clients wrote them and the attributes an SDK sends for each.
mcpSpans.session: session.id_hash is the keyed hash (the resource hash key, as principal ids are hashed) of the Mcp-Session-Id the server issued, never an id only a request carried; absent where the server issued none (stateless HTTP, stdio, the 2026-07-28 protocol). It needs agentrail.hash_key_id on the resource.
mcpSpans.payloads: request.payload (the request params) and response.payload (the result, or the error object) are sent only when the application turns payload capture on, which needs a redact hook, as JSON text after it; a hook that drops the payload sends neither, and one that fails or returns what is not JSON is the loss code payload_redact_failed. A request with no answer (a notification, a cancelled request) still sends its request payload. No length of ours bounds them, except that a span's two payloads together are cut to limits.mcpPayloadBytes (UTF-8, on a character boundary), the longer first, with its truncated flag set, so one span always fits an export. An SDK holds at most 64 MiB of payload text per queue (loss code payload_budget). The collector keeps them only for a source whose Admin turned payload capture on.

mcpRequestFacts.source: The header names, their order, Accept and Accept-Encoding of the two MCP clients the lab measured on 2026-11-04 (packages/journey-linkage/src/features/harness.ts, its two rows): Claude Code 2.1.318 on 620 of 620 MCP POSTs and Codex 0.166.0 on 557 of 557. Values other than those three, the bodies and the host are stand-ins. The Codex request also carries x-forwarded-for, as a load balancer appends it, which no reader takes as the caller's.

otlp.cliSpans: On the entry span of a request whose x-agentrail-cli header reads (cliHeader), a server SDK sets cliAttributes from what it said: name, version, command, run_id, sequence (an integer), mode, session.source, agent.name, agent.version, agent.evidence (the names, comma-joined) and sdk.version, each absent where the header has none; and session.id_hash, the keyed hash of the header's ses with the resource hash key, never ses itself. It needs agentrail.hash_key_id on the resource. A header that does not read sends no attribute. The collector takes them as the event's cli and names its session cli:<session.id_hash>:<the UTC day the span started, as days since the epoch>; facts outside what an event holds are not taken, and the event names cli (or cli.session) in redactions.

notes: What a customer's CLI says of itself on each request to its own API, written by agentrail-cli-sdk (and its Go and Python twins): an RFC 9651 Dictionary. v (Integer, the version, 1), sdk (String, the CLI SDK's version), cli and cliv (Strings, the CLI's name and version), run (String, a UUID minted for the run), seq (Integer from 1, the request's place in the run), ses (String, 32 lowercase hex: the session), sesfrom (Token: agent, ci, local or run), mode (Token: agent, ci, interactive or non-interactive), agent and agentv (Strings: the agent detected, lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', and its version), ev (Inner List of Strings: the names of the variables the agent or CI was told by, never their values, 1 to 8) and cmd (String: the command, by the words the CLI's code declared, never its arguments). Strings are printable ASCII, at most 64 characters (cmd 128). cliv, agent, agentv, ev and cmd are absent where unknown.

A later version only adds members and never changes what one means: a reader takes any v from 1, ignores the members it does not know (of any RFC 9651 type, Dates and Display Strings included), and reads nothing (no attribute, no cli) from a header that is not a Dictionary, misses a member, holds one outside these rules, or gives one twice, as two header lines a server joins into one value do.

ses is hex(SHA-256("agentrail-cli-session" NUL scope NUL sesfrom NUL source)), its first 32 characters. scope is the CLI's session scope (its name unless it names another). source is, for agent, the variable the agent names its own session in and its value as NAME=value; for ci, the CI service and the parts naming its run (sessionKeys); for local, the id of a session the CLI keeps for 30 minutes without a request and a day at most, in the file named by sessionFiles (hex(SHA-256(scope NUL agent-or-empty)), first 16 characters); for run, the run id.

A server SDK sends ses only as its keyed hash (keyedSession; cliSpans). The edge sends a CLI request as an event with cli set and session.id cli:<keyed hash of ses>:<the UTC day the request started, as days since the epoch>, in place of the visit cookie a CLI never sends back.

The CLI sends the header only to the origins it lists, and never what people type. A server SDK never sends it on in the requests its server makes; the edge passes it to the origin it stands in front of, whose server SDK reads it too.
